title: GroupBy, Pivot & Cohort Analysis
interviewAnswer: Grouping and pivoting turn event-level data into interpretable segment, cohort and time summaries. The key is choosing denominators and cohorts consistently.
keyPoints: Do not mix counts and rates without denominators.
why: GroupBy, Pivot & Cohort Analysis appears frequently in data-science work because it connects mathematical assumptions to practical decisions, diagnostics and failure modes.
deepDive: Grouping and pivoting turn event-level data into interpretable segment, cohort and time summaries. The key is choosing denominators and cohorts consistently. Do not mix counts and rates without denominators. Check Simpson’s paradox across segments. A strong practitioner separates the modeling assumption from the estimation procedure, checks diagnostics rather than trusting a single score, and explains what would make the method inappropriate.
workedExample: Build retention by signup month and weeks-since-signup rather than comparing raw active-user totals.
commonMistakes: Applying the method without checking its assumptions or data-generating process.
Choosing it because it is familiar rather than comparing against an appropriate baseline.
followUps: What assumptions does GroupBy, Pivot & Cohort Analysis make?
How would you validate or debug GroupBy, Pivot & Cohort Analysis in practice?
production: In production, validate assumptions on real data, monitor the quantities that can drift, and keep a simple baseline so added complexity has a measurable reason to exist.
